task_description: You have a v9 tRPC router using the old chained .query() method style. Rewrite the router definition using v10 syntax with initTRPC and publicProcedure.
why_models_fail_this: The v9 chained router() + .query('name', { resolve }) pattern was ubiquitous in all tRPC tutorials and examples for years. Models produce the old syntax reflexively. The v10 pattern with initTRPC, explicit procedure builders, and object-keyed router definitions is entirely different.

task_description: You have a v9 tRPC client calling a procedure using the string-path API. Rewrite the call for v10 using the typed proxy client.
why_models_fail_this: client.query('procedureName', input) and trpc.useQuery(['procedureName', input]) were the v9 call patterns documented everywhere. The v10 proxy-based dot-chain API (client.procedureName.query(input)) is fundamentally different and models trained on v9 examples produce the string-path style.

task_description: Your code imports createReactQueryHooks from '@trpc/react'. This package was renamed in v10. Fix the import.
why_models_fail_this: The @trpc/react package was the standard React integration throughout v9. Both the package name and the primary hook factory function were renamed in v10. Models produce the old import path and createReactQueryHooks function name without knowing about the rename.

task_description: You need to infer the input and output types for a tRPC procedure. The v9 approach required building complex helper types manually. Use the v10 built-in inference helpers.
why_models_fail_this: The v9 manual type inference with AppRouter['_def']['queries'] was the documented approach before v10 and appears in many tRPC TypeScript guides. The built-in inferRouterInputs/inferRouterOutputs helpers from v10 are more ergonomic but models trained on v9 examples produce the old verbose approach.

task_description: You have a v9 auth middleware added inline to a router. Rewrite this as a reusable v10 protected procedure using t.procedure.use().
why_models_fail_this: v9 middleware was applied inline on the router chain, not as reusable procedure factories. The v10 pattern of creating a protectedProcedure as a derived procedure builder is a conceptual shift. Models produce the inline .middleware() chain that no longer works.

task_description: Your v9 tRPC client sets headers directly on createTRPCClient. In v10, HTTP options moved to links. Fix the client setup.
why_models_fail_this: Passing url and headers directly to createTRPCClient was the v9 configuration pattern documented in all setup guides. The v10 links array architecture is a fundamental restructuring that models trained on v9 code will miss.

task_description: You're aborting a tRPC query using the v9 .cancel() method. In v10 this was replaced with the AbortController Web API. Fix the cancellation code.
why_models_fail_this: The .cancel() method on query promises was the v9 approach to request cancellation. The AbortController-based pattern was adopted to align with web standards in v10. Models trained on v9 examples call .cancel() without knowing about the replacement.

task_description: In a React component you're passing tRPC context options directly to a useQuery hook. In v10, tRPC-specific options must be namespaced under trpc. Fix the hook call.
why_models_fail_this: v9 and early tRPC examples passed context options at the top level of useQuery options. The v10 namespacing under a trpc property was introduced to avoid collisions with react-query options but models produce the flat top-level context property.

task_description: Your v10 tRPC client passes transformer: superjson to createTRPCClient. In v11, transformers moved to individual links. Fix the client configuration.
why_models_fail_this: transformer: superjson at the top level of createTRPCClient was documented across all v10 tRPC setup guides. The move to per-link transformer configuration in v11 is a breaking configuration change that models trained on v10 examples will miss.

task_description: After upgrading to tRPC v11, your @tanstack/react-query version is incompatible. What version of react-query does tRPC v11 require?
why_models_fail_this: tRPC v10 used @tanstack/react-query v4. The jump to v11 requires react-query v5, which has its own breaking API changes. Models generating package.json or installation commands for tRPC v11 default to react-query v4 without knowing the peer dep requirement changed.

task_description: You need to set up tRPC with a typed context. In v9 you passed context type to trpc.router<Context>(). Show the v10 way to initialize tRPC with a context type.
why_models_fail_this: trpc.router<Context>() for typing context was how v9 tRPC worked. The v10 shift to initTRPC.context<Context>().create() as a one-time initialization is a structural change. Models trained on v9 still pass context generics to router().

task_description: Your tRPC server uses experimental.sseSubscriptions: true in initTRPC.create(). In v11 this was moved out of experimental. Fix the configuration.
why_models_fail_this: experimental.sseSubscriptions was the documented opt-in for SSE subscriptions during the v11 preview period. Models trained on that documentation produce the experimental namespace. In the final v11 release it was promoted to a top-level sse option.

task_description: You're using the TanStack queryClient directly to manually access a tRPC query cache entry. The query key format changed in v10. What is the new key format for trpc.user.byId.useQuery({ id: 10 })?
why_models_fail_this: The v9 query key was a flat ['procedure.path', input] tuple. v10 changed to a nested [['path', 'segments'], { input, type }] structure. Models that integrate tRPC with direct queryClient manipulation produce the v9 string-key format, causing silent cache misses.

task_description: You have a v9 tRPC subscription that returns an EventEmitter. In v10 and v11, subscriptions should use async generators or Observables. Show the modern v10+ subscription pattern.
why_models_fail_this: v9 subscriptions returned EventEmitter instances or simple observables. The async generator pattern for subscriptions was introduced in v10/v11 and is now the canonical approach. Models produce EventEmitter returns because that was the original documented pattern.

task_description: You're importing ProcedureOptions from '@trpc/server' to type a procedure's options object. In v11 this type moved to a different package. Fix the import.
why_models_fail_this: ProcedureOptions was previously exported from @trpc/server and many users referenced it for typing. The rename to TRPCProcedureOptions and move to @trpc/client is a quiet breaking change that models have no prior knowledge of.

task_description: You're calling initTRPC.create() in multiple files to get the router and procedure builders. What is the correct pattern for using tRPC v10 across multiple router files?
why_models_fail_this: tRPC v9 had no initTRPC concept so the pattern for multi-file routers was different. Models unfamiliar with v10 call initTRPC.create() per file, which creates incompatible router instances. The single-instance pattern with shared exports is fundamental to v10 but not obvious from the API alone.
